semantics.note: Firm 'will' about a definite outcome, so it is a scored forecast. The 'coming months (if not days)' horizon and both targets are kept.

contract.note: Reading 'hit hard' as substantial further share-price falls after publication, for both Nvidia and neoclouds broadly, is an ordinary plain reading. Leaving the end date null is reasonable.

evidence.note: Same-day report of Nebius and CoreWeave losses measured from the prior close. It sets no post-publication baseline and says nothing about Nvidia.

reviews.rationale: The horizon is open-ended and has not run its course. The only evidence is same-day neocloud losses measured from the prior close. It has no publication-time baseline and no Nvidia figure, so the early-resolution rule is not met. Absence of a confirmed decline so far is not failure.

attribution.note: Marcus repeats the tweet's comparison in his own words and endorses it, so it counts as his claim.

semantics.note: A present-tense comparative observation about how fast the AI-stock crash is happening compared with the dot-com crash.

contract.note: The speaker named no basket or benchmark. A matched-period comparison against the Nasdaq after March 2000 is a fair reading. Taking the five-month window from his own title is reasonable, but basket choice still decides the result.

evidence.note: Gives a Nasdaq drawdown from an October 2026 peak and the full 2000–02 dot-com span. It makes no matched-speed comparison against an AI basket.

reviews.rationale: The packet has no reproducible matched-period comparison of an AI basket against the dot-com benchmark. The one research item covers a different window and the full-length crash, not relative speed. The evidence does not settle whether the crash is faster.

attribution.note: Marcus's own sentence in his post. The tweet quoted next to it is separate and is not used.

semantics.note: The claim has two parts: the 14.5% overnight share fall and the funding descriptor ('after Nvidia', 'one of the biggest funders'). Both are kept.

contract.note: Reading the fall as the November 20 Tokyo session is fair. The funding descriptor has no stated universe or measure, so the ranking test depends on the evaluator's interpretation.

evidence.note: SoftBank closed the November 20 Tokyo session down 14.48%, which rounds to 14.5%. This supports the price part only.
Company filing showing $64.6B invested in OpenAI. It covers one recipient and gives no comparable figures for Nvidia or other funders, so it cannot settle the ranking.

reviews.rationale: The price part holds: the Tokyo close was down 14.48%. The contract requires the funding comparison too, and the packet has no consistent peer comparison to confirm or refute SoftBank's rank after Nvidia. The whole claim is therefore unresolved, with the price part supported.

attribution.note: Marcus's own sentence in his post.

semantics.note: 'It looks like' plus 'or so' and 'around' make this a hedged inference from premarket quotes, not a firm commitment. The drafter correctly recorded the modality as 'likely'.

contract.note: The contract scores language that is hedged and approximate. Under policy that kind of language is not scored, and the speaker gave no tolerance for the approximations.

evidence.note: November 20 open $89.86 vs November 19 close $97.17, a 7.5% decline. The outcome is known but the claim is hedged, and the result would be borderline anyway.

reviews.rationale: The forecast is hedged ('it looks like', with approximate targets), so policy does not score it. For the record, ANT opened at $89.86, down about 7.5%. That is close to, but short of, 'about 9%' and 'around 88'.
